title: Support ticket triage
job: Support teams: route each inbound message to the right queue, flag same-day urgency and gauge frustration before an agent opens it.
why_this_mode: Zero-shot letters already score 0.768 on the closest measured workflow, and labels gathered from agents' corrections lift typed-decisions from 0.704 to 0.766 with 50 typical labels per question.

evidence.metric: typed-decisions, customer_service workflow (500 decisions): Gemma 4 12B Q8_0 zero-shot letters

limits: Evidence comes from typed-decisions customer-service threads, not your queue; Laya's fine-tuned checkpoint ties zero-shot there (0.764 vs 0.768), and score questions like frustration are the weakest zero-shot primitive (0.642).

title: Invoice routing for accounts payable
job: Accounts payable: decide approve, hold or reject for each vendor invoice and flag a missing purchase order or an amount mismatch.
why_this_mode: Zero-shot letters score 0.768 on the invoice workflow from day one, and the corrections clerks make on held invoices become the labels that fit a probe and a conformal gate.

evidence.metric: typed-decisions, invoice_processing workflow (500 decisions): Gemma 4 12B Q8_0 zero-shot letters

limits: Laya's checkpoint fine-tuned on typed-decisions scores 0.804 on the same invoice rows, and one forward pass is weak at arithmetic (JevBench hard temporal_numeric, 2 of 15), so compute totals and differences in code and pass them in the state.

title: Security alert triage
job: Security operations: label each alert's category and severity and decide whether the on-call analyst looks at it now.
why_this_mode: Zero-shot letters reach only 0.688 on the security workflow, security teams already hold dispositioned alerts to train on, and a labelled probe reaches 0.750 on this workflow (0.793 across all four).

title: AI agent trace review
job: Teams running AI agents: check each run against its instructions and budget and decide whether a person reviews it before its results are used.
why_this_mode: Agent traces are the weakest workflow for zero-shot letters (0.594), and a probe trained on reviewed runs reaches 0.736 there, level with Laya's fine-tuned 0.732.

title: Intent and tool router
job: Teams building in-app assistants: send each request to one of many intents or tools, and know whether it needs the user's own account.
why_this_mode: With 77 intents, zero-shot needs a five-pass tournament (0.713 at 589 ms p50), while a probe trained on 2,000 labelled requests answers in one pass at 0.860, close to Jev's published 0.870.

evidence.metric: Banking77 (400 test rows, 77 intents): Gemma 4 12B Q8_0 zero-shot letters, chunked tournament (5 passes)

ms per decision, p50, Banking77 tournament, RTX 5080 laptop

limits: Banking77 stands in for your intents; the probe needs about 26 labelled requests per intent on average and was measured in-process at layer 22 of the full 4B, not on the served 24-block file.

title: Prompt-injection guard
job: Anyone putting an LLM in front of untrusted text: flag user messages, retrieved pages and tool results that try to override the model's instructions.
why_this_mode: Zero-shot letters beat every Laya checkpoint on held-out injections (0.759 against at best 0.672), but about one in four answers is still wrong, so log the misses and fit once labels exist.

limits: Measured on 116 rows of one public dataset with an ECE of 0.167 as shipped (0.240 at T = 1); the technique question, new attack styles and the gain from learning on this task are not measured, so use it as one layer of defence.

title: Multilingual assistant intents
job: Assistant builders serving many languages: map an utterance in any supported language to one intent without training a model per language.
why_this_mode: Zero-shot letters score 0.885 macro across 11 languages, above an English-trained probe (0.803) and Laya's multilingual checkpoint (0.524), so nothing needs training per language.

title: Voice commands while you speak
job: Desktop and accessibility builders: start the right action from a spoken command before the user has finished speaking.
why_this_mode: The action list is a cached prefix, so each new word costs about 30 ms of compute, and the class-aware commit policy acted early with 1 harmful action in 198 utterances.

evidence.metric: 220 authored English commands, the same 16 actions (data/voice/): intent accuracy on the final transcript, Gemma 4 12B Q8_0

out-of-scope requests answered 'none': precision

limits: Measured on 220 authored English commands and synthetic speech, not on real microphones or accents; compound commands need a second decision on the rest of the transcript, and the 30 ms figure needs llama-server's --swa-full.

title: Passage check for RAG
job: RAG pipelines: drop retrieved passages that cannot answer the question before they reach the answer step.
why_this_mode: A yes/no judgement over a passage is the primitive Tez measures best zero-shot (BoolQ 0.850, typed-decisions yes/no 0.812), so filtering can start without labels.

limits: BoolQ measures answering a yes/no question from a passage, not judging whether a passage contains the answer, so relevance filtering itself is not measured, and each passage costs one pass (136 ms p50 on BoolQ).
